caption: A long barbecue lighter is clicked, and a small flame appears at its tip and burns steadily.

sa.check: A flame appears at its tip.
The flame is at the tip rather than the handle.
The press comes first and the flame follows.

pc.expect: The flame appears at the tip at the moment the trigger is pressed and goes out when it is released.
pc.fail: The flame is alight before the trigger is pressed; or the trigger is pressed and no flame appears at all; or the flame stays alight after the trigger is released; or the flame appears at the handle rather than the tip.

pc.expect: The flame points upward however the lighter is tilted.
pc.fail: The flame points downward; or leans along the lighter's barrel as it is tilted; or hangs below the tip; or points at the hand whatever way the lighter is held.

pc.expect: Once lit the flame burns steadily while the trigger is held and does not go out and relight by itself.
pc.fail: The flame goes out and relights with the trigger still held; or grows and shrinks in turn with the trigger held steady; or drifts away from the tip and burns in the air; or splits into two flames.

pc.expect: The lighter stays a rigid wand and the flame is a soft tongue of light at its tip.
pc.fail: The lighter's barrel bends or droops near the flame; or the flame holds a fixed rigid shape like a blade; or the lighter melts; or the flame casts solid pieces.

pc.expect: One lighter with one tip; the lighter keeps its shape and the hand passes through nothing.
pc.fail: A second tip or flame appears; or the lighter vanishes; or the hand passes through the lighter; or the lighter changes into another object.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The lighter's body, its trigger and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The lighter changes colour; or the trigger moves to a different place; or the background changes between frames.
